t: Jay Miner's Ghost & RMS's Vision: Bootstrapping a New Amiga
s: This article explores the philosophical underpinnings of vendor lock-in, historical tech ironies (Newton vs. Palm, ARM's origins), and the 'Craft of Elves' versus 'Game of Orcs' archetypes in technology creation, contrasting individual creation with zero-sum competition. It delves into the Free Software movement, specifically the role of Guix and Guile as GNU's extensibility dream rooted in LISP.
sub: Vendor lock-in: Data Gravity vs. Experience Gravity
Historical tech irony: Newton's failure enabling ARM's success
Archetypal conflict: 'Craft of Elves' (creation) vs. 'Game of Orcs' (competition)
GNU/Guix/Guile: LISP's legacy, extensibility, and the Free Software movement
